title: Buildings the City rents whose owner pays no property tax on them
question: Which buildings the City rents carry a welfare, religious or other exemption, so that the landlord collects City rent on property the City does not tax?
finding: 9 rented sites carry an exemption on the 2026-27 roll, $353,304,129 of exempt value in all; the largest is 845 Jackson Street (welfare, $232,196,298).
how: Buildings matched to a Board file with the City as tenant or to the Real Estate Division lease report of April 2025; exemption code and misc. exemption value from the 2026-27 workbook, described with the workbook's own code key. Rent is as the parcels screen read it from the Board file title, where the title states it.
limits: An exemption applies when the property is used for the exempt purpose; a nonprofit that rents part of its building to the City for a public service may still qualify, and the welfare exemption covers affordable housing run by nonprofits. The roll does not say which part of a building is exempt or who the tenant of that part is. The Assessor's exemption claim file (form BOE-267 and its supporting lease list) would show whether the City's space was claimed as exempt. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).

columns.t: Year’s rent in a lease file

sources.t: San Francisco Assessor-Recorder, secured property roll workbooks, roll years 2018-19 to 2026-27 (sf.gov property assessment data, saved by hand)
San Francisco Board of Supervisors, legislation files (Legistar)
